messages.subject: Plausible Values
parts:
Is there a way to obtain Plausible Values estimates of factor scores with mirt?

Bets regards,
Tomasz

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Plausible Values
parts:
All factor scores (from the fscores() function) are technically 'plausible values', but I assume you mean the large scale methodology for comparing different groups? No, this hasn't been implemented yet since it would require a separate function to a) draw the plausible values, b) apply the user defined relationship between the drawn values (e.g., lm(), lme(), etc), and c) pool the values via multiple imputation methodology.

I have plans to add this sometime, but since it's primarily for sparse large scale data it hasn't been high on the todo list. 

Phil

messages.author: 571bc49ad5c5fb80
messages.subject: Re: Plausible Values
parts:
I mean "first step" of this methodology :) I think that your plans regarding implementation of PVs is rather ambitious in the sense, that typically software is simply returning PVs, leaving user alone with conducting further analysis in a proper way (and besides lets note, that we generate PVs to enable some other people to perform some analysis in the future, without estimating our latent trait model). And for me it would be enough. Generally, analysis using PVs is rather something to be included in another package - if someone wants to make one.

Besides, I guess that returning PVs is "almost implemented". That is, what fscores() is doing when called with argument MI>1, is drawing (MI) PVs from posterior distribution (of each response pattern) and returning their mean. If this guess is wright, I would be pleased if I could ask fscores() not to average, but to return a set of draws for each observation/response pattern.

Tomek

On Tue, Oct 21, 2014 at 12:19 PM, Tomasz Żółtak <to...@gwozdzie.dhs.org> wrote:
I mean "first step" of this methodology :) I think that your plans regarding implementation of PVs is rather ambitious in the sense, that typically software is simply returning PVs, leaving user alone with conducting further analysis in a proper way (and besides lets note, that we generate PVs to enable some other people to perform some analysis in the future, without estimating our latent trait model). And for me it would be enough. Generally, analysis using PVs is rather something to be included in another package - if someone wants to make one.
Interesting point. I'll keep that in mind if I really do choose to go down this approach.

Besides, I guess that returning PVs is "almost implemented". That is, what fscores() is doing when called with argument MI>1, is drawing (MI) PVs from posterior distribution (of each response pattern) and returning their mean. If this guess is wright, I would be pleased if I could ask fscores() not to average, but to return a set of draws for each observation/response pattern.

Not quite. The MI option here is a different methodology, which imputes variability of the theta estimates based on parameter variability (not posterior distribution of theta). Mostly, this is useful when the number of items is quite small, or the calibration sample size results in imprecise parameter estimates. 

I suppose adding a 'posterior_draws = #' argument to fscores() to return a list of imputed values from the posterior is possible, and probably the best way to to approach the problem. I'll consider adding this to the dev version sometime. Thanks for the suggestion.

Phil

Tomek

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Plausible Values
parts:
I've added plausible value imputation support to fscores(), as well as latent regression models more generally to mirt() on the current dev version (1.6.6). 

The values are drawn assuming that each posterior is shaped like a multivariate normal distribution, which to me seems like a perfectly reasonable assumption about the shape of each individual posterior anyway (it's generally implied when you fit IRT models, and is one inspiration for using adaptive quadrature integration in the literature). 

If you are interested in checking this out before the next major release, feel free to update directly from Github. Cheers.

Phil
